summary: Plan revision 7 and contract AC-8 preserve approved PRD v0.2 product scope. The bridge-owned runtime-info validator and one-read wrapper are internal evidence and data-minimization work supporting the existing runtime, verification, and local diagnostics objectives. Fixed redacted invalid-schema and read-failure outcomes do not add a user-facing feature, browser route, authentication classification, host-health claim, or new execution authority. The plan retains all PRD AC-01–18 and full release criteria. No material product contradiction or unsupported scope addition was found.
review_boundary: Fresh read-only product-scope review of the registered PRD v0.2 against the current build-delivery revision 7 plan, AC-8 contract, runtime-info design boundary, and recorded user approvals. This verdict concerns document coherence and scope only.
verification_limits: The prior approval binds PRD v0.2 and the continuation approval binds spec-index v0.3 for implementation, technical probes, local-browser build, verification, and local monitoring within that PRD. Neither approval establishes that the new AC-8 code or runtime behavior works.

The pinned-client probe uses injected synthetic fetch. Its one-request and zero-ambient-fetch observations can support validator behavior for those fixtures, but do not prove OS network isolation, a live SDK host, ownership, availability, version compatibility, authentication, control-channel security, recovery, or product readiness.

The two new AC-8 checks are partial evidence mapped in the plan and contract to AC-2/4/6/8 and AC-2/4/7/8 respectively. Existing E2E and operational drills use synthetic local fixtures and cannot complete PRD AC-01–18 or actual monitoring obligations by themselves.
All 10 packet document hashes, plan and contract hashes, and approval target/evidence hashes matched disk. No implementation, app tests, service, or live SDK host was run for this review.
